name: Bespoke
zh_summary:
After a wondrous first half for investors, especially for those in growth stocks, the second half of 2026 has been a struggle.  The Russell 3,000 -- which represents roughly 98% of publicly traded US stock market cap -- is up about 3% in the 2nd half, but the average stock in the index is actually down 4.4%.

Along with rising interest rates hurting the most interest-rate sensitive areas of the market, it appears as if the shorts are betting big and winning these days.

We broke the Russell 3,000 into deciles (10 groups of roughly 300 stocks each) based on each stock's short interest as a percentage of its equity float.  We then calculated the average 2nd half percentage change of the stocks in each decile.

Decile one in the chart below all the way to the left of the image, contains the decile of most heavily shorted stocks in the Russell 3,000.  Stocks in this decile are down an average of 13.6% in the 2nd half.  As short interest levels get smaller, performance gets better, and the two deciles containing the least heavily shorted stocks are actually averaging gains in the 2nd half.

During big market rallies, shorts feel the pain and usually push prices higher as they rush to cover.  We're definitely not in that type of environment now, and we haven't been for months.

On the flip side, as the shorts get more confident from their winning ways, the spring gets coiled further.  The next time we get a positive market development that brings investors back into equities, be it

name: Gary Black
zh_summary:
Contrary to what many on X believe, I am not a $TSLA hater.  From 2019-2023, $TSLA was my largest position.  In investing, valuation vs price has to matter and if you’re not regularly calculating the difference, you’re not a serious investor. My issue with $TSLA now is that price seems high relative to my estimate of value, so I either wait for future earnings and cash flows to move higher (they are declining right now - see below), or for the stock price to move lower to become attractive again.  

$TSLA stock has significantly underperformed NDX over the past 1, 3, and 5 years, as 2026-2030 earnings estimates have declined, as automation has become a commodity, and as valuation became stretched.  So no, I’m not a TSLA hater;  I just don’t care for the current price relative to my estimate of value.

name: The Kobeissi Letter
zh_summary:
AI will become one of the largest spending categories in the US economy:

AI services are projected to account for a record 8.8% of US GDP in 2032.

This estimate shows how much businesses and consumers are expected to spend per year on the services of AI companies.

This also implies AI companies would generate ~$3.5 trillion in annual revenue by 2032.

By comparison, US consumer spending on food accounts for a similar 9.1% of GDP.

This figure would also be ~72% higher than energy, at 5.1% of GDP, and twice the size of construction as well as computers and software, both at 4.4%.

It would also be nearly 3x defense, at 2.8%, and more than 7x communications and internet, at 1.2% of GDP.

The only category where spending is significantly larger is health, at 18% of GDP.

The scale of the AI revolution is unlike anything seen before.
